_comment: Mutation testing on the trust-critical modules (issue #187, part of #178). Diff-coverage proves changed lines EXECUTE; mutation testing proves the tests would CATCH a bug. Scope is deliberately limited to the highest-stakes pure logic: trust derivations (app/trust), the manual-entry dedup matcher (app/server/listings/dedup.ts), and the write rate limiter (app/server/rate-limit). ignoreStatic is ON (AUB-201): static mutants — mutations in module-level initialization, where perTest coverage can't apply so EACH ONE re-runs the whole suite — were, per Stryker's own MutantTestPlanner warning on the CI run that prompted this, 60 mutants (13%) consuming an estimated ~92% of the runtime (the local re-measure below counted 56 static of 454 generated); ignoring them cut the run from tens of minutes to ~5m22s. TRADE-OFF: static mutants are now UNSCORED, so this gate no longer exercises module-level constants (e.g. RECENT_INCIDENT_WINDOW_DAYS, DEFAULT_STALENESS_MONTHS, DEFAULT_WRITE_RATE_LIMIT, the CLAIM_ATTRIBUTE_* maps). The highest-stakes ones stay pinned by ordinary hardcoded-literal tests that Stryker never ran for them anyway: the 90-day incident window (trust-model.invariant.test.ts), the rate-limit config (rate-limit/index.test.ts toEqual({limit:50,windowMs:60_000})), and staleness-window growth (summary.test.ts's literal 7-month check); a shrink of DEFAULT_STALENESS_MONTHS to 3-5 is the one unpinned direction, accepted because it fails SAFE (flags staleness earlier, never later). Ignored static mutants leave the score's denominator, so the baseline was RE-MEASURED with ignoreStatic on: total mutation score 84.62% across 403 runtime mutants (summary 97.04, browse-glance 96.77, browse-card-format 95.24, rate-limit 84.21, dedup 71.88, incident-recency 62.50 — the last dragged down by Zod error-message string literals and TZ paths the DB-free suite can't fairly kill). thresholds.break is 84 (rounded DOWN from 84.62) so it PASSES today on a green main and can be ratcheted up as tests improve — it is intentionally NOT set above the measured score, which would false-fail a green main. To raise the floor, add tests that kill surviving mutants (see reports/mutation/mutation.html) and bump break. BASELINE NOTE (AUB-258): the 84.62%/403-mutant figures above were measured BEFORE the TypeScript 7 bump broke this gate. The current measurement is 84.50% across 413 scored mutants — see tsconfigFile_comment. `thresholds.break` is still 84 and still passes, but it is justified by the stale number; re-baseline it rather than trusting the 84.62 above.
tsconfigFile_comment: AUB-258 workaround, NOT a normal setting. This points at a file that does not exist ON PURPOSE. TypeScript 7 (PR #320) removed ts.parseConfigFileTextToJson, which @stryker-mutator/core still calls from TSConfigPreprocessor, so the job crashed before running a single mutant. NO released Stryker fixes this: 10.0.0 (published 2026-08-14) carries the identical call at ts-config-preprocessor.js:46, and pinning TypeScript back would revert #320 repo-wide. That preprocessor exists only to rewrite paths that would escape the sandbox, and it skips the removed API entirely when the tsconfig is not found in the project, so an unresolvable path sidesteps the crash. PRECONDITION, and it is the whole reason this is safe: tsconfig.json here uses NEITHER `extends` NOR `references`, AND its include/exclude/files entries all resolve inside the repo root. The preprocessor rewrites all five, so if any of them ever points outside the repo, revisit this. Verified on this branch: 2 TypeErrors before, 0 after; full run exit 0, mutation score 84.50 vs break 84 (349 killed of 413 scored). REMOVE THIS and restore the default tsconfigFile once Stryker ships a TypeScript 7-compatible release.
